$comment: The sky's cloud layer (docs/CLOUDS.md, ADR 0034, Phase 31): a thin deck at a fixed altitude drawn in the sky, its shape a domain-warped fBm, lit by the sun and the moon. Run `node shared/look/clouds.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-look/src/clouds.gen.rs is stale.

deck.$comment: altitudeM: the deck's height above sea level, on the viewer's face. curvatureM: the radius of the sphere the deck lies on (smaller: the deck meets the horizon nearer). crossFadeM: the deck fades out as the eye comes within this of it, from below or above, and insideFog fades in instead: the view mixed toward the cloud colour by the density of the cloud the eye is in (0–1). horizonFade: the elevation sine over which clouds fade in above the horizon. fadeStartM/fadeEndM: the distance along the view ray over which clouds fade into the sky's haze. rimMarginM/rimFadeM: the deck and the volume are only over the world's disc (BUGS.md #101): out to its radius (the world size's, sent at join) plus rimMarginM from the disc's axis, fading out over the last rimFadeM, so nothing floats in the void beyond the rim.

shape.$comment: scaleM: the size of the largest noise cell (m). wrapM: the noise repeats every this many metres (a multiple of scaleM; keeps the shader's f32 coordinates small far from the origin). octaves/lowOctaves: noise octaves on High and Low. gain: each octave's weight relative to the last. warp: how far the domain warp moves a point (in cells). coverage: the share of the sky covered, 0 (clear) to 1 (overcast); the renderer can override it at run time (weather). edgeSoftness: the width of a cloud's soft edge, in noise value. opacity: the densest cloud's opacity.

wind.$comment: The clouds drift at speedMps toward directionDeg (degrees from +X toward +Z); the warp field drifts at evolveMps toward evolveDirectionDeg, so the shapes change slowly as they go.

light.$comment: sRGB tints of the frame's lights (the renderer's sun, moon and sky ambient colours, so the clouds follow whatever sets the lights): sunlit (the sun's) and shade (the day sky's ambient) by day, nightLit (the moon's) and nightShade (the night sky's ambient) by moonlight, sunset the warm tint of a low sun. absorption: how fast light dims through cloud. shadowStepM: how far toward the light the self-shadow samples. shadowOctaves/lowShadowOctaves: the octaves of the deck's self-shadow sample toward the light on Medium and High (the deck they draw in reflections and Snell's window) and on Low (the 2D deck in the sky: phones, and while the volume's noise bakes); 0 none, at most the tier's octaves. The sample is what makes the deck read 3D: sun-facing edges lit, far edges and thick undersides shaded (docs/CLOUDS.md §10). silverLining/silverPower: the bright rim of thin cloud near the sun or moon, and how tight it is around it. sunWarmth: how much a low sun tints the clouds. topLight: how much less light the deck's top loses through the cloud, seen from above (bright sunlit tops).

volume.$comment: The volumetric layer (docs/CLOUDS.md §8): ray-marched between baseM and topM above sea level on the viewer's face, when the Clouds setting's tier has steps (tiers). Density: the shape model (form, weather, cloudTypes; docs/CLOUDS.md §9). nearM: within this of the layer (or inside it) a tier marches with its nearSteps at its nearDivisor (BUGS.md #90). extinction: the view ray's opacity, the light lost per metre at density 1 along the view (what hides a cloud behind another; `?cloudExtinction=` overrides it live for an A/B, docs/CLOUDS.md §9.8). lightExtinction: the same along the light's path toward the sun or moon (× light.absorption: how far light goes through a cloud: lit edges, the silver lining, the glow), separate so a more opaque view leaves the light alone. plumeExtinction: a plume's view opacity. sunsetShade: how much a low sun's warm tint (light.sunset, by the deck's ramp up to light.sunWarmth) also takes the shade (the sky's light and the ground's bounce), toward the deck's shaded side (sunset × 0.75), the mix capped at 1: 0 only the sun's light warms (the volume read near white at sunrise: its light is mostly the cool sky's), 1.5 the deck's warmth at its lit sides, bases warm too. maxDistanceM: the march's reach along the ray (the deck's fade still hazes it). Against the scene (§8.9): each texel marches only to the farthest scene pixel under it, and the composite takes a texel's cloud at a pixel where the texel ended within a band of the pixel's scene: the texel's depth range, at least depthBand and at most depthBandRange of the distance (soft out to twice the band). plumeBillow: how much rising 3D noise (cells the plume's own width, scrolled up at its riseMps) breaks a plume's density up (0: smooth). The light (§8.8): each sample is the sun's (or moon's) light plus the ambient. Sun: the tier's lightSteps samples toward the light, the first lightStepM long and each lightStepGrowth times the last (4 cover the layer's depth), give the optical depth; Beer's law over it (light.absorption), with multiScatter the floor of light that still reaches deep inside (a wider, weaker Beer for light scattered many times), a powder term (powder: thin edges facing away from the light a little darker), a dual-lobe Henyey–Greenstein phase (phaseForward the forward lobe's g: the silver lining toward the light, phaseBack the back lobe's g, phaseBackWeight its share, phaseStrength how much the phase shapes the light, 0: even all round) times sunStrength. Ambient: the shade colour (the sky's light) from above, skyAmbient at a cloud's top, dimming with the cloud above the sample (half every ambientDepthM × ln 2 of cloud), and groundBounce of it tinted by bounceTint from below, dimming with the cloud under the sample: so bases are darker than tops. With no light samples the cloud above the sample stands for the light's path.

form.$comment: The clouds' shape (docs/CLOUDS.md §9, after Schneider's Nubis): tiling 3D noise baked once when a volume tier first draws (in the job workers): the base texture baseSize³ (RGBA8: a Perlin-Worley and three octaves of Worley fBm) repeating every baseTileM, the detail texture detailSize³ (a finer Worley fBm, the curl across, a blue-noise tile for the march's jitter) repeating every detailTileM (the curl's field every curlTileM). Base shape: remap(Perlin-Worley, -(1 - Worley fBm), 1) × the cloud type's height profile, then remap(·, 1 - cover, 1) × cover, the weather map's cover (the deck's noise soft-cut by the coverage over coverageSoftness). Edges eroded by the detail fBm × detailErosion (the core stays), the fBm inverted above wispHeight of the layer (wispy bases, billowy tops) and its point moved by the curl up to curlM metres (most at the base). shear: how far (m) the shape leans downwind per metre up (wind.directionDeg). The tiles must divide shape.wrapM.

weather.$comment: The weather map (docs/CLOUDS.md §9.2), per column from the deck's noise: cover (the deck's coverage, soft-cut over form.coverageSoftness), the cloud type (0-1 along cloudTypes' at: type, plus typeFromCoverage × how far the column's noise is past the coverage's cut, so a cloud's core towers higher than its edges, plus typeVariation × a second noise, -1 to 1) and precipitation (0-1: thicker, darker cloud, × each type's darkening at its base). A weather system will drive these at run time; today they are the data's.

tiers.$comment: Per Clouds setting value: the march's steps per pixel (0: the 2D deck, as before), the light samples per step toward the sun or moon (0-6; 0: the cloud above the sample stands for the light's path), the march's resolution divisor (1 full, 2 half, 4 quarter: the march draws into a buffer that size, accumulated over frames and upsampled by the composite) and how much of each new frame goes into the accumulated picture (historyBlend: lower is smoother, slower to follow). The CPU adapter draws no clouds (clouds_for). plumeSteps: the samples through each plume the ray crosses (0: no plumes; docs/CLOUDS.md §8.7). nearSteps/nearDivisor: the steps and divisor while the eye is within volume.nearM of the layer or in it (more samples and resolution where the clouds are close: BUGS.md #90); at least steps, at most divisor.

sources.$comment: Run-time plume sources (docs/CLOUDS.md §8.7), each the look of the plumes a game system adds: lavaVent the faint steam over a lava vent's active lake (over its molten surface, radiusM wide at its base widening by spread, heightM tall, rising at riseMps; removed when its lava is gone).
